summary: American painter Thomas Kinkade, the self-styled Painter of Light, sold mass-produced, lightly retouched prints as investments through a Christian-branded gallery franchise that ruined its owners, while groping employees before dying of an overdose in 2012.

evidence.note: born January 1958 in Sacramento, raised in Placerville by a single mother
Bakshi hires Kinkade and Gurney to paint backgrounds for the 1983 film Fire and Ice
by 1989 he wins startup money from an investor by overstating his print sales
prints dabbed with paint by hired highlighters marketed as unique, appreciating investments
casts art critics as liberal elites, selling his prints as a culture-war stance
1994 IPO of Lighthouse Publishing and the rise of its share price
stock allegedly driven down before he took the firm private; 2006 arbitration award to gallery owners
member of a Bush presidential prayer team; art framed as conservative ideology
2002 South Bend gathering where he gropes a gallery employee, per arbitration testimony
after his separation, a DUI arrest, jail time and repeated relapses
dies April 2012 at 54 of alcohol and Valium intoxication
estate fight, the company continuing after his death and a study on disliking his art
